traced the browser-session control flow by hand: `ctx = None` then `try: ctx, pg = open_editor_ready(...)` -- the call is INSIDE the try block; `except Exception as e` catches ANY exception from open_editor_ready through the click sequence and re-reports it via the same 'note-publish-live: REFUSED ... unexpected browser-session error occurred: {e}' stderr shape as every other gate, never a bare re-raise; `finally: if ctx is not None: try: ctx.close() except Exception: pass` -- if open_editor_ready itself raises before returning, the tuple assignment never completes, ctx stays None, and finally correctly skips closing what was never held (no double-close, no crash on a None context)

traced open_editor_ready() by hand: launch_context() result is immediately wrapped in try; add_cookies/new_page/goto/the readiness poll are all inside that try; the except clause closes ctx (best-effort, its own try/except around ctx.close()) THEN re-raises -- a partially-launched context can never be orphaned regardless of which of the two callers (note-publish-live.py or note-set-single-price.py) invokes it
